claims.text: The local catalog models Battle Road Spring 2002 regional third place prize as one unnumbered promotional source row containing No.3 Trainer at source index 249.
Bulbapedia says the 2002 No.3 Trainer Battle Road Spring print was awarded to third-place winners of each regional Battle Road Spring 2002 tournament, held between March and April 2002.
Bulbapedia says the Battle Road 2002 series was the first to introduce the Master age division for players 18 and over, in addition to Junior and Senior divisions.
Bulbapedia says the 2002 No.3 Trainer versions were the last to include the winner's name and regional conference on the card itself and the last to feature male and female variants.
Bulbapedia gives the Battle Road Spring 2002 No.3 Trainer text as recognizing and praising the third place winner of the Pokémon Card Game Official Tournament 'Battle Road Spring 2002'.
Bulbapedia says the Battle Road Spring 2002 tournaments did not feature a Best in Japan final; top ranking players instead earned byes in Battle Road Summer 2002.
PokeBoon's exact Battle Road Spring 2002 No.3 Trainer page lists Ken Sugimori as illustrator; this is useful collector-reference support, not primary-source print authority.

Pokumon's Battle Road 2002 research reconstructs Spring 2002 No.3 Trainer distribution as 4 girls and 50 boys from Trainers Magazine winner data; this is a collector estimate, not an official copy count.

Bulbapedia's Ken Sugimori page says there are many Pokémon TCG cards illustrated by Sugimori, though most include reused artwork from games, and indexes his broad official artwork role in the franchise.

As judged collector texture, this No.3 Trainer matters because third place widens the record: the card preserves the broader podium, not only the champion myth, and gives agents another rank-specific route to keep exact.

Agents should preserve No.3 rank, Battle Road Spring 2002 regional third-place route, source index 249, e-Card Era layout, winner name and regional conference fields, male/female variant boundary, Spring-vs-Summer distinction, and non-equivalence with No.1/No.2 Trainer or other No.3 Trainer eras before accepting a match.

narrative.human_title: Battle Road Spring 2002 No.3 Trainer: the edge of the podium still speaks
narrative.why_it_matters: No.3 Trainer is where the trophy story becomes more humane. First place is mythic, second place is tense, but third place shows the apparatus trying to remember more people. This row is still personal: name, conference, variant, rank, and region all matter. It tells an agent that recognition in Pokémon was not only a single summit; it was a structured field of placements, and every placement has its own evidence.

narrative.human_title: No.3 Trainer, Spring 2002: the full podium becomes visible
narrative.why_it_matters: The third-place card makes the system feel less like a single grail and more like a real tournament. It is not just below No.1 and No.2; it completes the shape of the podium.
